summary: Added patch::write_chart_edits with support for borrowed and trait-object writers, complete pre-write validation, typed error sources, and direct streaming of unchanged XML slices. Added nine integration tests; all required checks passed.

commands.outcome: Exit 2 during discovery because the tests directory did not yet exist; skill/SKILL.md was listed. Created the permitted integration-test directory afterward.
Passed (exit 0); formatted implementation and integration tests.
Passed (exit 0): 165 existing unit tests, 9 new integration tests, 0 doc tests; no failures or ignored tests.

design_decisions: A private ValidatedSplices owns only planned replacement fragments and borrows input XML. It checks every range, sorts with the existing (start, end, sequence) ordering, and checks all overlap before exposing chunks.

Both public chart-edit APIs use the same plan_chart_edits function and chunk iterator. Existing structural fragment construction uses the same validation type. The streaming path never invokes the full-document Vec-producing API or clones the whole XML.

The new W: std::io::Write + ?Sized bound accepts both concrete writers and &mut dyn Write while retaining caller ownership. write_all handles short writes, Interrupted and WriteZero; no flush or close occurs.

WritePatchError owns the original PatchError or io::Error. Manual Display and Error implementations require no new dependency. An additive Error implementation for PatchError enables typed Error::source downcasts. Custom I/O payload identity is tested.
Validation failures precede every writer call, including late invalid and overlapping spans. I/O failures stop immediately and may leave a prefix; documentation explicitly disclaims rollback.

Existing public signatures, enum variants, exhaustive matching and struct-literal construction remain unchanged. Only the new error enum is non_exhaustive. Existing inline tests and configuration were preserved.

Integration coverage includes every ChartEdit variant, value and label replacement, identity and empty edits, same-anchor series appends, mixed point/series growth, short and interrupted writes, trait objects, byte preservation, validation atomicity, WriteZero, and custom I/O failures at multiple output positions.
limitations: This is a component-level implementation and test run in the supplied minimal workspace; no full document engine, renderer visual comparison, upstream integration, or performance/allocation benchmark was performed.

As in the existing APIs, ChartData must come from scanning the same XML bytes. The new output phase validates all planned splice ranges; it does not introduce a complete independent validator for arbitrarily forged ChartData.
Planner replacement and structural clone fragments still allocate as permitted. Streaming removes the extra full-result buffer but is not allocation-free.
The supplied Rust 1.93.1 toolchain and cached dependencies were used. No toolchain, dependency, manifest, or lint-configuration changes were made.
